# Keep One Resolution: full page text

> Complete text of keeponeresolution.com: every page, plus the full bank inside its free quiz.
> The quiz picks one New Year's resolution you can keep. Four questions, about one minute.
> Free forever. No ads, no accounts. Your answers stay in your browser.
> Text captured from the live site, 2026-11-03; thirteen page sections added from the live pages on 2026-11-06, five more on 2026-11-06 for the wave-2 pages, and three more on 2026-11-06 for the wave-3 pages: all fifty-one sitemap pages now have a section.

Pick my one resolution
How it works
You pick one area. Body, money, home, work, family, calm.
You say what felt hard. And what made past plans fail.
You pick your time. Thirty minutes, two hours, or five.
You get one plan. One move, sized to your time.
You name week one. Day, time, place, person. Or skip it.
You name a favorite. One thing you already love. Your pick can ride on it.
One plan only. You get one, not a list of ten.
Your note stays here. It saves as a card on this device.

&middot; Open the full ask page

### The four questions

1. Pick one part of your life. Options: Body and health; Money; Home; Work; Family and friends; Mind and calm.
2. What was hard this year? Options: I felt drained a lot. Things piled up on me. I felt stuck in place. I drifted from good habits. I felt alone a lot.
3. How much time do you have each week? Options: 30 minutes a week; 2 hours a week; 5 hours a week.
4. What made past plans fail? Options: I tried to do too much. I just forgot to do it. Life got busy and loud. I got bored and quit.

### The bank: 30 actions, 90 resolutions

Each action below appears at three time levels, so the bank returns one of 90 resolutions.
Every result also carries a first move for week one, one note for when it gets hard (picked by question 4),
a weekly check-in prompt to copy into your own AI, and a year card with 52 dots, one for each week.

#### Body and health

- Take a short walk (when you felt: I felt drained a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Take a short walk: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 5 min right after a meal.
  - 2 hours a week: "Take a short walk: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 15 min right after a meal.
  - 5 hours a week: "Take a short walk: 30 min, 7x a week." First move: Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 15 min right after a meal.
- Cook a real meal (when you felt: Things piled up on me.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Cook a real meal: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Write one meal on a sticky note. Cook it tonight in about 15 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Cook a real meal: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Write one meal on a sticky note. Cook it tonight in about 15 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Cook a real meal: 60 min, 5x a week." First move: Write one meal on a sticky note. Cook it tonight in about 30 min.
- Do a short workout (when you felt: I felt stuck in place.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Do a short workout: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Lay out your clothes the night before. Do 5 min in your living room.
  - 2 hours a week: "Do a short workout: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Lay out your clothes the night before. Do 15 min in your living room.
  - 5 hours a week: "Do a short workout: 40 min, 5x a week." First move: Lay out your clothes the night before. Do 20 min in your living room.
- Stretch your whole body (when you felt: I drifted from good habits.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Stretch your whole body: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Roll out a mat or bath towel. Stretch slow for 5 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Stretch your whole body: 20 min, 5x a week." First move: Roll out a mat or bath towel. Stretch slow for 10 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Stretch your whole body: 20 min, 7x a week." First move: Roll out a mat or bath towel. Stretch slow for 10 min.
- Walk with a friend (when you felt: I felt alone a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Walk with a friend: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 15 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Walk with a friend: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 15 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Walk with a friend: 45 min, 5x a week." First move: Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 25 min.

#### Money

- Check your bank balance (when you felt: I felt drained a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Check your bank balance: 2 min, 3x a week." First move: Open your bank app after breakfast. Check the balance for 2 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Check your bank balance: 5 min, 3x a week." First move: Open your bank app after breakfast. Check the balance for 5 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Check your bank balance: 5 min, 5x a week." First move: Open your bank app after breakfast. Check the balance for 5 min.
- Sort bills in one spot (when you felt: Things piled up on me.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Sort bills in one spot: 20 min, 1x a week." First move: Gather all bills into one box. Pay one due bill. Move $5 to savings.
  - 2 hours a week: "Sort bills in one spot: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Gather all bills into one box. Pay one due bill. Move $5 to savings.
  - 5 hours a week: "Sort bills in one spot: 30 min, 2x a week." First move: Gather all bills into one box. Pay one due bill. Move $5 to savings.
- Move cash to savings (when you felt: I felt stuck in place.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Move cash to savings: 2 min, 1x a week." First move: Set a $5 auto move for payday. It moves each week by itself.
  - 2 hours a week: "Move cash to savings: 2 min, 2x a week." First move: Set a $5 auto move for payday. It moves each week by itself.
  - 5 hours a week: "Move cash to savings: 2 min, 3x a week." First move: Set a $5 auto move for payday. It moves each week by itself.
- Write down what you spend (when you felt: I drifted from good habits.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Write down what you spend: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Keep one list on your phone. Write down each spend that day.
  - 2 hours a week: "Write down what you spend: 10 min, 5x a week." First move: Keep one list on your phone. Write down each spend that day.
  - 5 hours a week: "Write down what you spend: 10 min, 7x a week." First move: Keep one list on your phone. Write down each spend that day.
- Tell a friend your goal (when you felt: I felt alone a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Tell a friend your goal: 15 min, 2x a week." First move: Text one friend your money goal today. Ask them to check in Friday.
  - 2 hours a week: "Tell a friend your goal: 30 min, 2x a week." First move: Text one friend your money goal today. Ask them to check in Friday.
  - 5 hours a week: "Tell a friend your goal: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Text one friend your money goal today. Ask them to check in Friday.

#### Home

- Tidy one small corner (when you felt: I felt drained a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Tidy one small corner: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick the corner by the front door. Tidy only it for 5 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Tidy one small corner: 20 min, 4x a week." First move: Pick the corner by the front door. Tidy only it for 10 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Tidy one small corner: 20 min, 7x a week." First move: Pick the corner by the front door. Tidy only it for 10 min.
- Clear one shelf fully (when you felt: Things piled up on me.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Clear one shelf fully: 25 min, 1x a week." First move: Pick the fullest shelf you have. Clear it fully in about 15 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Clear one shelf fully: 30 min, 2x a week." First move: Pick the fullest shelf you have. Clear it fully in about 15 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Clear one shelf fully: 30 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick the fullest shelf you have. Clear it fully in about 15 min.
- Fix one small thing (when you felt: I felt stuck in place.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Fix one small thing: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Write down the fix that bugs you. Start it. Give it 15 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Fix one small thing: 45 min, 1x a week." First move: Write down the fix that bugs you. Start it. Give it 25 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Fix one small thing: 45 min, 3x a week." First move: Write down the fix that bugs you. Start it. Give it 25 min.
- Make one room cozy (when you felt: I drifted from good habits.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Make one room cozy: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Pick the room you sit in most. Add one lamp or soft blanket.
  - 2 hours a week: "Make one room cozy: 60 min, 1x a week." First move: Pick the room you sit in most. Add one lamp or soft blanket.
  - 5 hours a week: "Make one room cozy: 60 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick the room you sit in most. Add one lamp or soft blanket.
- Have a friend visit (when you felt: I felt alone a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Have a friend visit: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Text one friend and pick a day. Come as you are. Just talk.
  - 2 hours a week: "Have a friend visit: 60 min, 2x a week." First move: Text one friend and pick a day. Come as you are. Just talk.
  - 5 hours a week: "Have a friend visit: 60 min, 3x a week." First move: Text one friend and pick a day. Come as you are. Just talk.

#### Work

- Plan your day on paper (when you felt: I felt drained a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Plan your day on paper: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Put paper and pen by your coffee. Write your top three tasks first.
  - 2 hours a week: "Plan your day on paper: 10 min, 5x a week." First move: Put paper and pen by your coffee. Write your top three tasks first.
  - 5 hours a week: "Plan your day on paper: 10 min, 7x a week." First move: Put paper and pen by your coffee. Write your top three tasks first.
- Clear your desk top (when you felt: Things piled up on me.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Clear your desk top: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Set a timer for 5 min. Clear the desk top into one box.
  - 2 hours a week: "Clear your desk top: 15 min, 4x a week." First move: Set a timer for 10 min. Clear the desk top into one box.
  - 5 hours a week: "Clear your desk top: 20 min, 5x a week." First move: Set a timer for 10 min. Clear the desk top into one box.
- Learn one work skill (when you felt: I felt stuck in place.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Learn one work skill: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick one small skill for your job. Learn it for 5 min today.
  - 2 hours a week: "Learn one work skill: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Pick one small skill for your job. Learn it for 15 min today.
  - 5 hours a week: "Learn one work skill: 60 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick one small skill for your job. Learn it for 30 min today.
- Chat with a work friend (when you felt: I drifted from good habits.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Chat with a work friend: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Ask one work friend for coffee. Chat for 5 min this week.
  - 2 hours a week: "Chat with a work friend: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Ask one work friend for coffee. Chat for 15 min this week.
  - 5 hours a week: "Chat with a work friend: 30 min, 5x a week." First move: Ask one work friend for coffee. Chat for 15 min this week.
- Eat lunch with coworkers (when you felt: I felt alone a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Eat lunch with coworkers: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Ask two coworkers to lunch today. Eat together. Leave phones in pockets.
  - 2 hours a week: "Eat lunch with coworkers: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Ask two coworkers to lunch today. Eat together. Leave phones in pockets.
  - 5 hours a week: "Eat lunch with coworkers: 45 min, 5x a week." First move: Ask two coworkers to lunch today. Eat together. Leave phones in pockets.

#### Family and friends

- Talk with family at home (when you felt: I felt drained a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Talk with family at home: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick a time right after dinner. Talk at the table for 5 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Talk with family at home: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Pick a time right after dinner. Talk at the table for 15 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Talk with family at home: 60 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick a time right after dinner. Talk at the table for 30 min.
- Share one meal together (when you felt: Things piled up on me.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Share one meal together: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Pick one dinner this week together. Eat at the table. No phones there.
  - 2 hours a week: "Share one meal together: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Pick one dinner this week together. Eat at the table. No phones there.
  - 5 hours a week: "Share one meal together: 60 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick one dinner this week together. Eat at the table. No phones there.
- Play one game together (when you felt: I felt stuck in place.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Play one game together: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick a short game from the shelf. Play one round tonight together.
  - 2 hours a week: "Play one game together: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Pick a short game from the shelf. Play one round tonight together.
  - 5 hours a week: "Play one game together: 60 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick a short game from the shelf. Play one round tonight together.
- Call a friend you miss (when you felt: I drifted from good habits.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Call a friend you miss: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick the friend you miss most. Call them today, right after dinner.
  - 2 hours a week: "Call a friend you miss: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Pick the friend you miss most. Call them today, right after dinner.
  - 5 hours a week: "Call a friend you miss: 30 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick the friend you miss most. Call them today, right after dinner.
- Visit someone you love (when you felt: I felt alone a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Visit someone you love: 30 min, 1x a week." First move: Text them today and pick a day. Visit soon and stay a while.
  - 2 hours a week: "Visit someone you love: 60 min, 2x a week." First move: Text them today and pick a day. Visit soon and stay a while.
  - 5 hours a week: "Visit someone you love: 60 min, 4x a week." First move: Text them today and pick a day. Visit soon and stay a while.

#### Mind and calm

- Sit in a quiet place (when you felt: I felt drained a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Sit in a quiet place: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Pick one quiet spot in your home. Sit there 5 min, no phone.
  - 2 hours a week: "Sit in a quiet place: 20 min, 5x a week." First move: Pick one quiet spot in your home. Sit there 10 min, no phone.
  - 5 hours a week: "Sit in a quiet place: 20 min, 7x a week." First move: Pick one quiet spot in your home. Sit there 10 min, no phone.
- Write thoughts on paper (when you felt: Things piled up on me.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Write thoughts on paper: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Put a notebook by your bed. Write for 5 min before sleep.
  - 2 hours a week: "Write thoughts on paper: 20 min, 5x a week." First move: Put a notebook by your bed. Write for 10 min before sleep.
  - 5 hours a week: "Write thoughts on paper: 20 min, 7x a week." First move: Put a notebook by your bed. Write for 10 min before sleep.
- Read a calm book (when you felt: I felt stuck in place.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Read a calm book: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Put your book on your pillow now. Read 5 min in bed tonight.
  - 2 hours a week: "Read a calm book: 30 min, 4x a week." First move: Put your book on your pillow now. Read 15 min in bed tonight.
  - 5 hours a week: "Read a calm book: 60 min, 5x a week." First move: Put your book on your pillow now. Read 30 min in bed tonight.
- Breathe slow in fresh air (when you felt: I drifted from good habits.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Breathe slow in fresh air: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Step outside your front door today. Breathe slow for 5 min.
  - 2 hours a week: "Breathe slow in fresh air: 10 min, 5x a week." First move: Step outside your front door today. Breathe slow for 5 min.
  - 5 hours a week: "Breathe slow in fresh air: 10 min, 7x a week." First move: Step outside your front door today. Breathe slow for 5 min.
- Sit outside with others (when you felt: I felt alone a lot.)
  - 30 minutes a week: "Sit outside with others: 10 min, 3x a week." First move: Sit outside with others after lunch. Stay 5 min and just talk.
  - 2 hours a week: "Sit outside with others: 20 min, 5x a week." First move: Sit outside with others after lunch. Stay 10 min and just talk.
  - 5 hours a week: "Sit outside with others: 30 min, 5x a week." First move: Sit outside with others after lunch. Stay 15 min and just talk.

### The four notes for when it gets hard

- I tried to do too much. -> Do just this move all month. Add more next month, not now.
- I just forgot to do it. -> Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
- Life got busy and loud. -> Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
- I got bored and quit. -> Same move, new place or playlist. Change one thing, not the move.

### The weekly check-in prompt (template)

The prompt copies as one short block. It names your action in short form. Shape, shown with the first bank entry:

Weekly check-in for my resolution.
My one resolution: Take a short walk.
Sessions this week: ___ of 3 (10 min each)
How many walks did I finish this week?
Which walk felt best this week?
What got in my way?
What is one small move for next week?
Please keep your reply short and kind.

## Privacy (https://keeponeresolution.com/privacy)

Privacy - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
Privacy
Your quiz plan stays in your browser.
Cloudflare and PostHog count visits to this site.
There is no account or email signup.
What the quiz saves
Finishing the quiz saves your four answers and result.
The result includes its check-in and share text.
The save uses this browser's local storage.
Your answers and plan stay on this device.
Anyone using this browser can open it.
The quiz code uses local storage, not cookies.
The result screen also offers a letter card.
Writing a note saves that note too.
It saves the open date you picked.
Your note is never sent to us.
Clearing your saved plan
Open your saved plan and tap Start over.
That button removes the saved answers and result.
It removes your saved note too.
Browser site-data controls can remove it too.
Copying and sharing
Copy buttons place text on your clipboard.
The site does not send copied text anywhere.
You choose where to paste copied text.
Sharing starts only when you tap Share.
Site counts
This page loads Cloudflare Web Analytics.
It sends page and performance counts to Cloudflare.
Cloudflare says its beacon uses no cookies.
Cloudflare says its beacon does not read local storage.
The home page also runs PostHog.
PostHog counts page views and quiz starts.
It counts finishes, shares, and return visits.
It counts check-in copies, lock-screen pictures, and letter cards.
Your note text is never sent to it.
Your quiz answers are never sent to it.
It does not record your screen.
Contact
Questions about privacy: hello@pickmyresolution.com.
Changes
Changes appear on this page.
Keep One Resolution. Built with Muse.

## Terms (https://keeponeresolution.com/terms)

Terms - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
Terms
The short version: This site gives one free plan.
What this site is
These terms cover this website only.
Keep One Resolution picks one resolution.
You answer four short questions.
The quiz picks one move for you.
Your plan fits the time you pick.
It is free forever.
There are no ads on this site.
There is no account or email signup.
Your plan
Your plan shows one resolution.
It shows a first move for week one.
It shows help if it gets hard.
It includes a weekly check-in prompt.
It includes share text you can copy.
You can make a lock-screen picture of your pick.
Ideas, not advice
Plans here are general habit ideas only.
They are not medical advice.
They are not mental-health advice.
They are not financial advice.
Use your own judgment with any plan.
Your saved plan
The quiz runs in your browser.
Finishing the quiz saves your four answers.
It also saves the result you see.
Your answers and plan stay on this device.
Cloudflare and PostHog count visits here.
PostHog counts quiz starts, finishes, and shares.
See the Privacy page for full details.
No guarantees
This site is provided as is.
We give no warranty.
We cannot guarantee any habit outcome.
We are not liable for any loss.
The site may have errors or downtime.
Fair use
Do not try to break this site.
Do not copy the whole action bank.
Do not claim our words as yours.
We may change or stop this site.
Contact
Questions about terms: hello@pickmyresolution.com.

## Question pages

### Why do New Year's resolutions fail? (https://keeponeresolution.com/why-do-new-years-resolutions-fail)

Why do New Year's resolutions fail? - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
Why do New Year's resolutions fail?
Most lists ask for too much, all at once. Last January, the list felt full of hope. By spring, none of it stuck.
Pick my one resolution
That fade is not a willpower problem. The plan was built to fade. Here are the four plain reasons, in the words people pick in our quiz.
Four plain reasons
I tried to do too much.
Five goals fight for the same week.
Each one steals time from the rest.
Soon the whole list feels too heavy to touch.
The counter the quiz gives you
Do just this move all month. Add more next month, not now.
I just forgot to do it.
The plan lived in your head.
No cue. No set time. No trigger.
By week two, whole days slipped past it.
The counter the quiz gives you
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Life got busy and loud.
One loud week breaks the chain.
Then the missed days feel like proof.
Proof that it failed, when it only bent.
The counter the quiz gives you
Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
I got bored and quit.
Same move. Same room. Same song.
Boredom starts to read as failure.
It is not failure. It is just boredom.
The counter the quiz gives you
Same move, new place or playlist. Change one thing, not the move.
What works: keep it small
Keep one. Size it to the week you really have. Start with one small first move.
That is the whole design of this site. Four short questions. One pick you can still be doing in March.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
Why do resolutions fail by February?
Most lists start too big.
January energy fades fast.
The plan has no room for a bad week.
One kept move beats a long list that fades.
Is failing a resolution a willpower problem?
No.
The plan was too big for the week.
A smaller plan fits real life.
Willpower was never the missing part.
What should I do with last year's list?
Read it once, kindly.
Pick the one item that still matters.
Make that one small enough to keep.
Let the rest go.

### How to keep a New Year's resolution (https://keeponeresolution.com/how-to-keep-a-new-years-resolution)

How to keep a New Year's resolution - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
How to keep a New Year's resolution
Keep one. That is the whole trick, and it is harder than it sounds. Last January, the list was long. This year, one pick, sized to your week.
Pick my one resolution
The method, in six steps
Step 1
Pick one, not a list
One goal gets your whole week behind it. A list splits that week five ways. Splitting is how good plans starve.
Step 2
Size it to your real week
Thirty minutes a week is a real plan. So are two hours a week. Pick the time you truly have, not the time you wish you had.
Step 3
Start with one small first move
Week one asks for one small move, not a new life. Here is a real pick from the quiz, word for word.
Picked for
I felt drained a lot. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Take a short walk: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 30 min right after a meal.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
Step 4
Plan for the hard day now
Hard days are part of the year. Pick your counter before you need it. The four counters live on our why resolutions fail
page.
Step 5
Check in once a week
Ask two short questions. Did I do my move this week? What got in my way? Your pick comes with a prompt you can copy into your own AI.
Step 6
Write a note to future you
Tell future you why this one matters. Save the note as a letter card. Read it when the year gets loud.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
How many resolutions should I keep?
One.
One fits a real week.
A list splits your time too thin.
You can add more next year.
What if I miss a week?
Do half at the next chance.
Half still keeps the streak.
One missed week is weather, not failure.
When should I start?
This week is fine.
Week one asks for one small move.
Small starts are the kind that last.

### What is a good New Year's resolution? (https://keeponeresolution.com/what-is-a-good-new-years-resolution)

What is a good New Year's resolution? - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
What is a good New Year's resolution?
A good one is small enough to keep in March. It names one move. It fits the time you really have.
Pick my one resolution
One real pick, start to finish
This is the exact card the quiz gives for one set of answers. Nothing here is dressed up.
Picked for
I felt drained a lot. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Take a short walk: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 30 min right after a meal.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
More real picks
Different lives, same shape. One move, one first step, sized to real time.
Picked for
I drifted from good habits. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Write down what you spend: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Keep one list on your phone. Write down each spend that day.
Picked for
Things piled up on me. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Clear one shelf fully: 25 min, 1x a week.
First move, week one
Pick the fullest shelf you have. Clear it fully in about 25 min.
Picked for
I felt alone a lot. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Visit someone you love: 60 min, 2x a week.
First move, week one

Picked for
Things piled up on me. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Clear your desk top: 15 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Set a timer for 15 min. Clear the desk top into one box.
What makes one good
One move. Not a list of ten.
Sized to real time. Your week, as it is.
A first step you can name today.
A plan for the hard day , picked early.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
What is a good resolution for a busy person?
One that fits 30 minutes a week.
The smallest real pick takes six minutes a week.
See the picks on our busy week page.
Should a resolution be big to matter?
No.
Small moves, done weekly, add up.
Big plans are the ones that fade by spring.
Can a quiz really pick a good one?
It asks four short questions.
What felt off. How much time you have. What failed last time.

Small New Year's resolutions - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
Small New Year's resolutions
Small is not a lesser goal. Small is the size that survives March.
Pick my one resolution
Last January, the list was long and grand. By spring, none of it had stuck. These picks skip grand on purpose.
The smallest of our picks
This card is a real quiz result. The answers: money felt stuck. The time: 30 minutes a week.
Picked for
I felt stuck in place. · 30 minutes a week
The pick

First move, week one
Set a $5 auto move for payday. It moves each week by itself.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses 2 of your 30 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.

### One resolution ideas (https://keeponeresolution.com/one-resolution-ideas)

One resolution ideas - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
One resolution ideas
You do not need fifty ideas. You need one that fits your week.
Pick my one resolution
Idea lists feel helpful. They change nothing. You skim fifty, save a few, keep none.
Last January proved that the hard way. This year gets one pick, chosen well.
How the quiz picks your one
Four short questions. Ninety possible plans. One answer.
It asks which part of life needs care.
It asks what this year felt like.
It asks how much time you truly have.
It asks what made past plans fail.
Then it returns one plan, not a list.

It ends with a note to future you. This one opens:
&ldquo;Dear future me, I felt drained a lot back then. My pick was Take a short walk.&rdquo;
You finish yours in your own words. It stays on your device.
Other pickers hand you fifty ideas. This one hands you one plan.
Pick my one resolution
Four questions. One pick, sized to your week.
The science under the plan
Four findings from real research shape every plan here:
If-then plans. Gollwitzer: "If 9am, then I walk" beats trying.
Tiny first steps. BJ Fogg: start so small it is hard to skip.
The fresh start effect. Dai, Milkman, and Riis: a new year lifts motivation.
Weekly check-ins. Watching your own record keeps the streak alive.
Your plan page lets you set each one yourself.
How it works
You pick one area. Body, money, home, work, family, calm.
You say what felt hard. And what made past plans fail.
You pick your time. Thirty minutes, two hours, or five.
You get one plan. One move, sized to your time.
You name week one. Day, time, place, person. Or skip it.
One plan only. You get one, not a list of ten.
Your note stays here. It saves as a card on this device.
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.

### What to do when you break your New Year's resolution (https://keeponeresolution.com/what-to-do-when-you-break-your-new-years-resolution)

What to do when you break your New Year's resolution - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
What to do when you break your New Year's resolution
A broken streak is data, not a verdict.
Pick my one resolution
You missed a day. Maybe a week. The old list would die here.
This one does not have to. Last January is not this January.
The restart rule
Keep the same one resolution.
Shrink the dose. Never swap the goal.
Restart at the next normal chance.
Not Monday. Not next month. The next chance.
Four ways back, by what broke
I tried to do too much.
Do just this move all month. Add more next month, not now.
I just forgot to do it.
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Life got busy and loud.
Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
I got bored and quit.
Same move, new place or playlist. Change one thing, not the move.
Those four notes are the quiz's own guards. Each pick ships with one.
A restart, start to finish
This restart sits at the smallest size. Ten minutes, three times a week.
Picked for
I felt alone a lot. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Sit outside with others: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Sit outside with others after lunch. Stay 10 min and just talk.
For when it gets hard
Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
More restarts at the smallest size
Family and friends
The pick
Talk with family at home: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Pick a time right after dinner. Talk at the table for 10 min.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
Home
The pick
Have a friend visit: 30 min, 1x a week.
First move, week one
Text one friend and pick a day. Come as you are. Just talk.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
Work
The pick
Clear your desk top: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Set a timer for 10 min. Clear the desk top into one box.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
Start again this week, at half size. A small kept year beats a grand quit.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.

Common questions
Is my resolution ruined after one miss?
No. One miss is weather.
Do half at the next chance.
The streak bends. It need not break.
Should I pick a new resolution instead?
No. Keep the same one.
Shrink its dose to fit your week.
A swap restarts the hard part.
When should I restart?
At the next normal chance.
Not Monday. Not next month.
The next chance is close enough.

### Realistic New Year's resolutions (https://keeponeresolution.com/realistic-new-years-resolutions)

Realistic New Year's resolutions - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
Realistic New Year's resolutions
Sized to a normal week. Two hours, not five.
Pick my one resolution
Most lists assume empty evenings and endless energy.
A realistic pick assumes neither.
It fits the week you already live.
Six realistic picks, one per area
Body and health
The pick
Cook a real meal: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Write one meal on a sticky note. Cook it tonight in about 30 min.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
Money
The pick
Check your bank balance: 5 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Open your bank app after breakfast. Check the balance for 5 min.
Your time
This plan uses 15 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Home
The pick
Tidy one small corner: 20 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Pick the corner by the front door. Tidy only it for 20 min.
Your time
This plan uses 80 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Work
The pick
Learn one work skill: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Pick one small skill for your job. Learn it for 30 min today.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
Family and friends
The pick
Share one meal together: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Pick one dinner this week together. Eat at the table. No phones there.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
Mind and calm
The pick
Read a calm book: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Put your book on your pillow now. Read 30 min in bed tonight.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
What realistic means here
One resolution only. Never a list.
Two hours a week, at most.
Split into short, normal sessions.
A first move for week one.
One guard for your hard days.
Two hours is the middle quiz answer.
Two plans here use even less.
Your pick will differ from these.
It will fit your answers, not theirs.

Smaller is easier, not more real.
Thirty minutes still counts fully.

### How to pick a New Year's resolution (https://keeponeresolution.com/how-to-pick-a-new-years-resolution)

How to pick a New Year's resolution - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
How to pick a New Year's resolution
Pick for the year you had. Not the year you wanted.
Pick my one resolution
Last January's list asked for everything.
This January, pick one thing well.
One action, three honest sizes
Say you felt alone a lot.
The action stays. Only the dose changes.
30 minutes a week
The pick
Walk with a friend: 30 min, 1x a week.
First move, week one
Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 30 min.
2 hours a week
The pick
Walk with a friend: 30 min, 4x a week.
First move, week one
Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 30 min.
5 hours a week
The pick
Walk with a friend: 45 min, 5x a week.
First move, week one
Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 45 min.
Pick your real time, honestly.
Four choices make the pick
One: Pick one part of your life.
Two: Name what was hard this year.
Three: State your real weekly time.
Four: Name what broke past plans.
Six areas. Five feelings. Three time sizes.
Thirty actions hide behind those choices.
A finished pick, start to finish
Picked for
I drifted from good habits. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Chat with a work friend: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Ask one work friend for coffee. Chat for 10 min this week.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
Notice what the card never does.
It never asks for five things.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words

Common questions
How many resolutions should I pick?
One. Only one.
A list splits your attention thin.
One pick gets your whole year.
What if two areas both feel urgent?
Pick the one that hurt most.
The other area waits, not dies.
Next year can hold it.
Does the quiz pick for me?
Yes. Four questions, one pick.
The pick fits your four answers.
Change an answer, change the pick.

New Year's resolution template - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolution template
Copy it. Fill it. Keep one.
Pick my one resolution

This template is that rhythm, on paper.
The template, filled with a real pick
Picked for
Things piled up on me. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Write thoughts on paper: 20 min, 5x a week.
First move, week one
Put a notebook by your bed. Write for 20 min before sleep.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses 100 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.

Weekly check-in for my resolution.
My one resolution: Write thoughts on paper.
Sessions this week: ___ of 5 (20 min each)
How many nights did I write?
What thought came up most?
What got in my way?
What is one small move for next week?

Or keep it in a notebook.

Sessions this week: ___ of ___
What got in my way?

The blanks stay the same all year.

It opens in 30 days.
Or in 90 days, or Dec 31.
The note stays in your browser.
This pick's note, word for word
Dear future me,
Things had piled up on me then.
My pick was Write thoughts on paper.
The pace was 20 min, 5x a week.
My notebook waits right by my bed.
I hope you still notice that small start.
The hard part was plain forgetting, some days.
Did the small move still fit my week?
From past me.

### What is Quitter's Day? (https://keeponeresolution.com/what-is-quitters-day)

What is Quitter's Day? - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
What is Quitter's Day?
The day most plans wobble. Yours can bend instead.
Pick my one resolution
Quitter's Day is January's second Friday.
In 2027, it falls on Friday, January 8.
The name came from fitness app data.
Early January effort drops sharply then.
A pick built for that week
This pick sits at the smallest size.
Ten minutes, three times a week.
Picked for
I felt stuck in place. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Read a calm book: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Put your book on your pillow now. Read 10 min in bed tonight.
For when it gets hard
Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
Why that week feels hard
The holiday glow has faded.
Work and school are back fully.
The plan still feels brand new.
One missed day feels like failure.
None of that means you quit.
It means week two is the test.
Your plan for that Friday
Keep the same one resolution.
Shrink the dose that week.
Do half after any miss.
Mark the week. Then keep going.
The day passes. The pick stays.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words

When is Quitter's Day in 2027?
Friday, January 8, 2027.
It is January's second Friday.
Eight days into the new year.
Does Quitter's Day mean I failed?
No. It names a common wobble.
Keep your one. Shrink its dose.
A bent streak still counts.
Where did the name come from?
Fitness app data showed the drop.
Activity fell sharply that Friday.
The name stuck after that.

### Should you tell people your New Year's resolution? (https://keeponeresolution.com/should-you-tell-people-your-new-years-resolution)

Should you tell people your New Year's resolution? - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
Should you tell people your New Year's resolution?
Tell one friend. Not everyone. Not nobody.
Pick my one resolution
Yes. Tell exactly one friend.
Keep it off public feeds.
When telling a friend is the pick
Picked for
I felt alone a lot. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Tell a friend your goal: 30 min, 2x a week.
First move, week one
Text one friend your money goal today. Ask them to check in Friday.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses 60 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
That pick exists for one feeling.
The year felt lonely, often.
Why one friend works
One friend can ask real questions.
One friend notices missed weeks.
Everyone knowing adds pressure, not help.
Nobody knowing makes quitting silent.
The quiz builds telling in.
Not a side tip. The plan itself.
Your pick, ready to send
Share text, word for word
My 2027 resolution:
Tell a friend your goal: 30 min, 2x a week.
First move: Text one friend your money goal today. Ask them to check in Friday.
Pick yours at https://keeponeresolution.com/?via=share
Send it to one person only.
Ask for check-ins, not applause.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
Should I tell everyone I know?
No. Tell one trusted friend.
Ask for Friday check-ins instead.
Skip the public announcement post.
What should my friend actually do?
Check in on Fridays.
Ask what got in the way.
Keep replies short and kind.
What if telling feels awkward?
Send the share text above.
It is already written for you.
One short text starts it.

### New Year's resolution to save money (https://keeponeresolution.com/new-years-resolution-to-save-money)

New Year's resolution to save money - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolution to save money
One saving pick. Two minutes at a time.
Pick my one resolution
Saving fails as a vague wish.
It works as an auto move.
The saving pick, start to finish
Picked for
I felt stuck in place. · 5 hours a week
The pick
Move cash to savings: 2 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Set a $5 auto move for payday. It moves each week by itself.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses 6 of your 300 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Six minutes of your week.
The rest stays entirely yours.
Why an automatic payment works
Memory fails. Auto moves do not forget.
The payment leaves on payday, so you do not have to remember it.
Five dollars proves the system works.
Grow the amount, not the count.
Other sites list twelve money tips.
Twelve tips become zero kept moves.
What this page is not
Not a budget overhaul plan.
Not investment or debt advice.
One move, repeated all year.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
How much should I save first?
Five dollars, moved by itself.
That is the engine's first move.
Raise it later, if it holds.
Do I need a budget first?
No. This pick comes first.
Sorting bills is a different pick.
One pick at a time here.
What if a week goes wrong?
Your alarm marks session days.
Missed weeks stay honest, not fatal.
Next week, the move runs again.

### New Year's resolution to exercise more (https://keeponeresolution.com/new-years-resolution-to-exercise-more)

New Year's resolution to exercise more - Keep One Resolution
Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolution to exercise more
Move more, in doses you keep.
Pick my one resolution
Exercise more is a wish.
These are its engine picks.
Three movement picks, real sizes
Picked for
I felt drained a lot. · 5 hours a week
The pick
Take a short walk: 30 min, 7x a week.
First move, week one
Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 30 min right after a meal.
For when it gets hard
Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
Your time
This plan uses 210 of your 300 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Picked for
I felt stuck in place. · 5 hours a week
The pick
Do a short workout: 40 min, 5x a week.
First move, week one
Lay out your clothes the night before. Do 40 min in your living room.
For when it gets hard
Same move, new place or playlist. Change one thing, not the move.
Your time
This plan uses 200 of your 300 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Picked for
I drifted from good habits. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Stretch your whole body: 20 min, 5x a week.
First move, week one
Roll out a mat or bath towel. Stretch slow for 20 min.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses 100 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Pick one card. Not all three.
One kept move beats three quit ones.
Why these three only
The health bank holds five actions.
Cooking is food, not exercise.
Walking with friends is social time.
These three move your body directly.
No outcome promised
No weight loss is promised here.
No fitness level is promised either.
Only sessions, sized to your week.

No. The workout happens at home.
Its first move says living room.
The stretch needs one towel.
What if I get bored?
Same move, new place or playlist.
Change one thing, not the move.
That guard ships with the workout.
How many sessions each week?
Each pick names its own count.
Seven walks. Five workouts. Five stretches.
Pick one count, not all three.

## Page: https://keeponeresolution.com/resolutions-you-should-not-keep

Keep One Resolution
Resolutions you should not keep
This site picks one resolution you can keep.
Pick my one resolution
First, the honest no.
Five moves live in your area. Four get a no, each with its reason. One is left standing.
One real showdown, start to finish
Say your year felt like this: Body and health. I felt drained a lot. 2 hours a week. I just forgot to do it.
Cook a real meal
30 min, 4x a week
This is the move for things piling up. You said you felt drained. Your weeks would go to the wrong problem, and the one you named would still be waiting.
Do a short workout
30 min, 4x a week
This one treats feeling stuck. Your words: you felt drained. On a hard day this is the first plan you would skip, because it was never about your day.
Stretch your whole body
20 min, 5x a week
The move for drifting from good habits. You named you felt drained instead. Nothing in your week would tell you it is working, because the change would happen somewhere you were not hurting.
Walk with a friend
30 min, 4x a week
That move answers feeling alone. Stated plainly: you felt drained. The mornings that made you pick this quiz would feel exactly the same.
The one left standing
Take a short walk
30 min, 4x a week
Built for feeling drained, in your words. Week one starts at 15 min. The plan below guards your weak spot.
First move, week one
Step 1: set a phone alarm. Step 2: Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 15 min right after a meal.
Your if-then
My cue: after lunch. Then I will take a short walk.
If it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
The four kinds of no
Big start. Tiny starts survive where big starts stall.
No slack. A plan with no slack snaps.
Payoff months away. Rewards you feel this week win. Distant payoffs lose to near ones.
Wrong feeling. Your weeks would go to the wrong problem.
Your four nos depend on your answers.
Get my honest no

What do I get after the nos?

A first move for week one.

## Page: https://keeponeresolution.com/do-new-years-resolutions-work

Keep One Resolution
Do New Year's resolutions work?
Yes, when they are built right. Here is the research, in plain words.
Pick my one resolution
In 2002, researchers tracked two groups for six months.
One group made a New Year's resolution.
The other wanted the same change, later.
At six months, 46% of resolvers were still succeeding.
Only 4% of nonresolvers were. (Norcross et al., 2002)
Making one, on its own, beat just wanting to change.
What the studies found
Finding 1: A start date gets you started
Big dates push people to begin.
Searches for "diet" rose 82.1% at a new year.
Gym visits rose 33.4% at a new week.
Researchers call this the fresh start effect.
It helps you start. It does not keep you going.
(Dai, Milkman and Riis, 2014, Management Science)
Finding 2: A habit takes about two months
96 people built one small daily habit.
It felt automatic after about 66 days, on average.
The range ran from 18 to 254 days.
Missing one day did not wreck the habit.
So January is the start, not the test.
(Lally et al., 2010, European Journal of Social Psychology)
Finding 3: Aim at something, not away from it
1,066 people were followed for a full year.
Approach goals beat avoidance goals, 58.9% to 47.1%.
"Walk after dinner" beat "stop snacking."
55% of responders called their year a success.
Success was self-reported, so read it with care.
(Oscarsson et al., 2020, PLOS ONE)
Finding 4: An if-then plan lifts your odds
A plan names the moment, then the move.
"If it is 7 pm, then I walk for 10 minutes."
Across 94 tests, plans lifted goal success.
The effect was medium to large (d = 0.65).
That is a big lift for one sentence.
(Gollwitzer and Sheeran, 2006)
The honest limits
Several studies rely on self-reported success.
Study volunteers may want change more than most.
No trick works for every person.
We found no real study behind the 92% failure claim.
The pattern still points one way.
One goal, aimed at a start, with a plan, tracked for two months.
Your options, built from this research
We built this site on these four findings.
Pick ONE resolution, not a list of ten.
Every pick is phrased as a start, not a stop.
Every pick comes with a first move for week one.
The tracker marks your first 66 days, week by week.
You can use the picker, which applies all four.
Or read the tracker page and run it on paper.
The science is shown above either way. The choice is yours.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
Do New Year's resolutions work at all?
Yes, for many people.
In one study, 46% of resolvers were still succeeding at six months.
Only 4% of nonresolvers were. (Norcross et al., 2002)
Is the 92% failure claim true?
No study we can trace says that.
The tracked studies land far higher.
Treat any bare failure rate with care.
What single change helps most?
Write an if-then plan.
Name the moment, then the move.
Across 94 tests, plans lifted goal success. (Gollwitzer and Sheeran, 2006)

## Page: https://keeponeresolution.com/how-long-do-new-years-resolutions-last

Keep One Resolution
How long do New Year's resolutions last?
About 3.74 months, on average, in one large survey. The full picture is kinder than the myth.
Copy the key points
Pick my one resolution
A Forbes Health and OnePoll survey asked 1,000 adults.
Their resolutions lasted 3.74 months, on average.
That is a survey of what people remembered.
Tracked studies tell a fuller story.
The timeline, study by study
Week 1 to 2
The drop starts fast.
January's second Friday is called Quitter's Day.
It names the wobble, not the end.
About 66 days
A new habit felt automatic at about 66 days.
The range was wide: 18 to 254 days.
Missing one day did not wreck it. (Lally et al., 2010)
Six months
46% of resolvers were still succeeding.
Only 4% of nonresolvers were. (Norcross et al., 2002)
One year
55% of responders called their resolution a success.
That was self-reported, in a study of 1,066 people. (Oscarsson et al., 2020)
Why the numbers seem to clash
Each study asks a different question.
One counts steady success, week after week.
One asks people to judge their own year.
Both can be true at once.
What they agree on matters more.
The first two months are the hard part.
Past them, the habit starts carrying itself.
How to be on the long side of the average
Keep one resolution, not five.
Size it to your real week.
Plan for 66 days, not 21.
After a miss, do half the next day.
Mark each kept week on the tracker.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
How long do New Year's resolutions last, on average?
About 3.74 months in one large survey.
That was a Forbes Health and OnePoll survey.
It asked 1,000 adults in the United States.
Why do the studies give different numbers?
They measure different things.
One tracked steady success at six months: 46%.
One asked people at one year: 55% said success.
Different questions, different answers.
When do most people quit?
The drop is steepest in the first weeks.
Week two even has a name: Quitter's Day.
Past about 66 days, a habit starts to feel automatic.

## Page: https://keeponeresolution.com/new-years-resolutions-for-students

Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolutions for students
One small pick that fits a class schedule. Not a list that dies by February.
Pick my one resolution
A student week is already full.
Classes, work, and sleep fight for the same hours.
So the pick has to be small and timed.
Here is one, in the picker's own shape.
One example pick for a student
Picked for
I felt stuck in place. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Learn one work skill: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Open one lesson right after your last class today.
For when it gets hard
Exam week? Do one 10 minute session. Keep the streak bent, not broken.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
That pick and dose come straight from the picker.
Ideas that fit a student week
Review today's notes for 10 minutes, same day.
Plan the week on paper, Sunday, 10 minutes.
Read one chapter ahead, before the lecture.
Keep one steady sleep time on school nights.
Save one small amount each week.
Walk to one class you now ride to.
Pick one of these. Only one.
A list of six is how February happens.
The if-then trick that fits school
Tie the pick to a moment that already exists.
"After my last class, I review my notes for 10 minutes."
Plans like that lifted success across 94 tests. (Gollwitzer and Sheeran, 2006)
Your timetable becomes the reminder.
Pick my one resolution
Or say it in your own words
Tell the ask page your year in a line or two. The same engine picks from your words.
Ask in your own words
Common questions
What is a good New Year's resolution for a student?
One that fits a class schedule.
Reviewing notes the same day is a strong one.
Ten minutes, three times a week, is enough to start.
How many resolutions should a student make?
One.
A term already carries a full load.
One small pick survives exam weeks. Five do not.
What if I fall behind during exams?
Shrink the dose that week.
Do half, then return to full size.
A bent streak still counts.

Take a short walk: 30 min, 7x a week.

Put your shoes by the front door. Walk 15 min right after a meal.
For when it gets hard
Miss a day? Do half the next day. Half still keeps the streak.
Your time
This plan uses 210 of your 300 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
Seven walks a week means daily.
The dose still stays thirty minutes.
Same pick, other sizes
At 30 minutes a week: 10 min, 3x a week.
At 2 hours a week: 30 min, 4x a week.
Start at the size you can keep.
You can grow it next month.

Text one friend and pick a day. Walk and talk for 15 min.
For when it gets hard
Do just this move all month. Add more next month, not now.
Your time
This plan uses all 120 minutes you offered.
Pick one card. Not both.
One kept walk beats two quit ones.

How many walks did I finish this week?
Which walk felt best this week?

Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolution to stress less
Fresh air. Slow breaths. Ten minutes.
Pick my one resolution
Stress less is a wish.
These picks give it air and quiet.
The breathing pick, start to finish
Picked for
I drifted from good habits. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Breathe slow in fresh air: 10 min, 5x a week.
First move, week one
Step outside your front door today. Breathe slow for 5 min.
For when it gets hard
Same move, new place or playlist. Change one thing, not the move.
Your time
This plan uses 50 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
That pick comes straight from the picker.
Outside the front door counts as outside.
Same pick, other sizes
At 30 minutes a week: 10 min, 3x a week.
At 5 hours a week: 10 min, 7x a week.
Ten minutes is the whole session.
Five short breaks beat one long one.
The quiet pick, for drained days
Picked for
I felt drained a lot. · 30 minutes a week
The pick
Sit in a quiet place: 10 min, 3x a week.
First move, week one
Step 1: set a phone alarm. Step 2: Pick one quiet spot in your home. Sit there 5 min, no phone.
For when it gets hard
Set a phone alarm for session days. Same time, same sound.
Your time
This plan uses all 30 minutes you offered.
Pick one card. Not both.
One kept plan beats two quit ones.

How many fresh air breaks happened?
When did breathing feel slowest?

Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolution to finish home projects
One small fix. Done fully.
Pick my one resolution
Finish the house projects is a wish.
This site shrinks it to one fix.
The fix pick, start to finish
Picked for
I felt stuck in place. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Fix one small thing: 45 min, 1x a week.
First move, week one
Write down the fix that bugs you. Start it. Give it 25 min.
For when it gets hard
Do just this move all month. Add more next month, not now.
Your time
This plan uses 45 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
That pick comes straight from the picker.
The list shrinks one fix at a time.
Same pick, other sizes
At 30 minutes a week: 30 min, 1x a week.
At 5 hours a week: 45 min, 3x a week.
Pick the size your week can hold.
A small fix done beats a big list.
One honest note
No whole house is fixed on this page.
No room redo is promised here.
Only one small fix, finished fully.
The next fix waits on your list.
Two check-in questions from the picker
Which small thing did I fix?
What fix comes next on my list?
The picker asks these each week.
They keep the list moving, one fix.

## Page: https://keeponeresolution.com/new-years-resolution-to-stretch-more

Keep One Resolution
New Year's resolution to stretch more
A mat. Slow moves. No rush.
Pick my one resolution
Stretch more is a wish.
This pick gives it a mat and time.
The stretch pick, start to finish
Picked for
I drifted from good habits. · 2 hours a week
The pick
Stretch your whole body: 20 min, 5x a week.
First move, week one
Roll out a mat or bath towel. Stretch slow for 10 min.
For when it gets hard
Same move, new place or playlist. Change one thing, not the move.
Your time
This plan uses 100 of your 120 minutes a week. The rest of your time stays yours.
That pick comes straight from the picker.
A bath towel works as a mat.
Same pick, other sizes
At 30 minutes a week: 10 min, 3x a week.
At 5 hours a week: 20 min, 7x a week.
Pick the size your week can hold.
A small size kept beats a big size quit.
One honest note
No cure for stiffness lives on this page.
No set reach is promised here.
Only slow stretching, sized to your week.
Stop any move that hurts.
Two check-in questions from the picker
How many stretch sessions did I do?
Which part still feels tight today?
The picker asks these each week.
They keep the plan honest and small.
